WHAT WE MEASURE OURSELVES · EACH READING ON ITS OWN
There is no single Scintilla fear & greed number here any more. We hold 364 stocks, no options flow of our own and no exchange high/low counts, so an internal one-number index would be claiming to measure a market we cannot see. Every row below is a real measurement of a real thing, with its own source and its own age, and nothing is averaged into a headline.
INPUT	OUR READING	FEAR · GREED	SCORE	CNN	AGE	SOURCE

52-week highs vs lowsNO SOURCE	no source	
	—	0	—	needs NYSE new-high / new-low counts · not collected
How many stocks are upLIVE	102 of our 363 stocks are up today · 28% advancing	
	28	0	now	our 364-stock universe · one /quotes call · counted per stock, where CNN weighs by volume
Put / call ratioLIVE	put/call 0.78 · five-day average 0.82	
	73	49	44h	Cboe daily put/call (PCC) · chart API · session 2026-09-22 · five-day average · inverted
News voiceLIVE	+0.146 · 669 of 2000 headlines carried a scoring word · 24h	
	57	—	9m	the news table · every headline scored here (lm-v1) · 24h · every scored headline counts once
YouTube voiceLIVE	+0.58 net · 108 bullish / 29 bearish mentions · 63 tickers · 7d	
	98	—	23h	social_sentiment source=youtube (DB) · yt-lexicon-v1 · 7-day window
X voiceLIVE	+0.29 net · 1070 posts · 24h · ranked vs 21 earlier days	
	48	—	1h	X feed (/api/xfeed · Trading-list collector) · keyword lexicon per post · 24h · percentile vs the feed's own days
Each row is scored the way CNN scores its own: how far today sits from that input’s own average, measured in the size it normally moves — two of those steps either way is the end of the dial; volatility and put/call are inverted, because more fear belongs at the low end. The cnn column is CNN’s own component score, for comparison only.

Each channel counts once, whatever its volume, and a ticker’s lean is the average of the channel leans. The clips are the ticker-tagged ones the search collector files; the reading is over their titles, because no transcript rows exist in the database yet (youtube_transcripts and youtube_video_sentiment are both empty).
The collector’s own pooled number, over transcripts on the subscribed channels, still reads 98 across 231 mentions — pooled, so a channel that posts fifty clips a week carries it. That is the number this blend is meant to replace once per-video rows are written.

greed · 59
96 channels · 1070 items · 44 lean positive, 12 negative, 40 neither · mostly agreed (21% on the smaller side)
zerohedge +0.01 · 141
Mr_Derivatives -0.06 · 53
JesseOlson +0.22 · 49
unusual_whales +0.04 · 47
newsinvesting +0.54 · 41
StealthQE4 +0.06 · 34
Oculustrade +0.04 · 28
The_RockTrading -0.08 · 26
One handle, one vote. Each post gets a keyword lean (the same finance word list, with negation), a handle’s lean is the average of its posts, and the reading is the average of the handles.
NEWS
EVERY HEADLINE SCORED · 24 HOURS
greed · 57
Each headline is scored here against a finance dictionary (Loughran-McDonald plus the price verbs headlines use), a negator in the three words before a match flips it, and the score is the balance of the words that fired. 669 of 2000 headlines in the last 24 hours carried a scoring word; 994 carried none and are not counted as zero, and 337 asked a question. The old per-ticker roll-up (news_sentiment, 374 tickers, averaging 0.126) is shown on the NEWS page for comparison only — nobody can say how it was produced. Newest headline 9m ago. Not blended by outlet yet: a headline carries its site, so the room can group by outlet as soon as the per-headline rows are stored — until then every scored headline counts once, whoever published it.
HOW EACH VOICE IS MEASURED
YouTube. A scheduled job collects clips from the channels Alan subscribes to and from ticker searches, and files them in youtube_videos. For the subscribed channels it fetches the English transcript and counts finance keywords around each ticker mention — a word list with negation (yt-lexicon-v1), not an AI read — and writes one pooled row per ticker into social_sentiment over a 7-day window. The room’s own blend above reads the ticker-tagged clips’ titles instead, because it needs the channel behind each reading and the per-video table is empty.
X. A browser-side collector saves the posts on Alan’s Trading list and publishes them at /api/xfeed. Each post’s text is run through the same keyword list; a post is bullish, bearish or neither; the blend above averages handles.
News. Every headline in the last 24 hours is scored on this page against the finance dictionary shipped at /data/news-lexicon/lm-headline-v1.json — the words that fired are kept, so any number can be opened down to them. The old per-ticker roll-up is still in the database and is shown only for comparison.
What makes all three wrong. A keyword list cannot hear irony or a hedge. A question is caught only when the question mark is there ("is NVDA about to crash?" is scored and then left out of the total). Titles are written to be clicked. Nobody checks whether a channel was right last month, so a reliable voice and a noisy one count the same. Coverage is whatever the collectors happened to fetch, not a sample of anything.
WHAT THIS ROOM DOES NOT SEE
Options flow of our own, exchange 52-week high/low counts, advancing and declining volume (we count stocks, CNN weighs by volume), anything outside our 364-stock universe, and any market outside the US. The published gauges above are shown exactly as their publishers print them and are never mixed into one of our own numbers.
